question: A 30-week primigravida reports a gush of clear fluid from the vagina 2 hours ago; no contractions. Sterile speculum examination shows fluid in the posterior fornix. Which single investigation BEST confirms prelabour rupture of membranes (PROM)?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. A high vaginal swab is important for detecting chorioamnionitis but does not confirm PROM. It should be taken alongside, not instead of, fluid analysis.

answers.text: Ferning (crystallisation) of pooled vaginal fluid on a glass slide

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Amniotic fluid contains proteins that, when allowed to dry on a glass slide, form a characteristic fern-like crystallisation pattern (arborisation). This test has a sensitivity ~90% and specificity ~95% for PROM and is the gold-standard bedside confirmatory test.
Incorrect. A urine dipstick tests for urinary tract infection, not PROM. Urinary incontinence can mimic fluid loss and must be distinguished, but a dipstick does not confirm amniotic fluid.
Incorrect. CRP is a marker for infection/chorioamnionitis after PROM has occurred, not a diagnostic test for the rupture itself.

overallFeedback.feedback: For PROM confirmation: sterile speculum shows pooling → ferning on glass slide (arborisation) confirms. Avoid digital examination — it increases infection risk.

Well done. Ferning (arborisation) is the standard bedside confirmatory test for PROM. The pooling test (visible fluid in posterior fornix) supports the diagnosis; formal confirmation uses ferning or IGFBP-1/PAMG-1 point-of-care tests.
